messages.subject: Q-value problem
parts:
Hello Everyone,
               I have millions of reads but Just for this question I chosed these two records
> meth     
chr   start     end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2
chr1 1234567 1234567      +         1      0      1         2      2      0
chr1 1234568 1234568      +         1      1      0         1      0      1

> myDiff25p = get.methylDiff(myDiff, difference = 25,qvalue = 0.01)
> myDiff25p
 chr   start     end strand    pvalue     qvalue  meth.diff
chr1 1234567 1234567      + 0.3333333 0.00155631 -100.00000
chr1 1234568 1234568      + 1.0000000 0.00155631  100.00000

I tried fisher_exact test for both the rows manually (by making matrices and using the fisher.test) It shows the p-value is correct for both the cases (0.3333333,1.0000000).

But why is the qvalue same for all the pvalues? Can somebody please explain to me how are they calculated?

When I run

myDiff = calculateDiffMeth(meth, num.cores = 4)
 the qvalues are same (0.00155631) for all the million of rows.

When I set slim=F
myDiff = calculateDiffMeth(meth, num.cores = 4,slim=F)
 the qvalue is 1 for all the million of rows.

I have also attached the p and q values histograms for both slim=T and slim=F

I see a break in the histogram of p-values. Is there any other solution to it?



thanks
